the development of transgenic maize that is resistant to southwestern corn boroer and sugarcane borers.
the improvement of the tropical maize lines CML72 and CML216 by introducing the cry1B and cry1B-IAb genes.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new constructs developed in this study have the potential to be useful in a resistance management strategy against tropical pests.
the cry genes have been stably integrated into maize genome and the introduced genes have been transmitted to the T3 generation in Mendelian ratios.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new constructs and the transformation procedure developed in this study are efficient tools for the development of transgenic maize plants resistant to tropical pests and for the management of resistance in the field.
the cry1B and cry1Ab genes are active in the tropical maize hybrids, and that the translational fusion of cry genes is a useful tool for resistance management in maize.

the cry genes are expressed in tropical maize, and the transgenic plants are resistant to the target insects, the cry genes are transmitted and inherited in a predictable manner, and the resistance is stable in the T3 progenies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cry1B and cry1B-cy1Ab constructs are useful for developing transgenic maize plants that are resistant to southwestern corn boroer and sugarcane borers and to the fall army worm, the most important maize insect pests in the tropics.
we have developed transgenic maize lines that express a novel cry1B protein, a novel cry1Ba protein, or a fusion protein of both, which confer resistance to southwestern and sugarcane borers.
it is possible to develop a resistance to tropical pests in tropical maize by using the same genes that are used in temperate maize.
